newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX hits records, shrugs off France.
newsitem.headline: German DAX hits records, shrugs off France.

text.p: Germany's blue chip DAX index continued its ascent into record territory on Monday, showing itself resilient to the surprising left-wing win in the first round of the French parliamentary elections.

The 30-share DAX, trading thinly, was up 21.39 points, or 0.6 percent, at an intraday record of 3,623.58 points early in the floor session, having recovered from a dip during pre-bourse electronic dealings.
"Political events never have a long-lasting effect on markets," said one dealer. "We're looking for a relaxing day."
Dealers said activity was limited by Monday's market holiday in the United States and Britain and that no solid trend had emerged in the German share market.
As a result, a strong upward push could be driven by a small number of players, one dealer noted.
"With volumes as low as this, anything can happen. And people always want to be in on the rallies," he said.
Dealers attributed individual share moves to technical factors, noting particular interest in the chemicals sector, where Bayer AG was up more than three percent at 67.95 marks.

At the same time, dealers said there was still widespread talk of the need for a correction from the share market's current lofty heights, but noted that this was only likely to happen if other markets, chiefly Wall Street, led the way.
"As long as Wall Street's closed, we're not really going anywhere," a dealer said.
